prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Make a new portrait DRAWING of Jackie Leven around 1971 from the TWO ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPHS supplied, not from any previously generated illustration.
Image 1: primary facial likeness reference. Image 2: supporting facial and long-hair reference. Ignore the printed page, text, backgrounds and exact photographic arrangement.

Direction: an economical, partly unfinished charcoal-and-ink drawing, more abstract and less meticulously rendered than a traditional shaded portrait, while keeping the real facial structure fully recognizable. Clearly hand-drawn: varied pressure, searching lines, broken hatching, broad dragged side-of-charcoal marks, dry brush streaks with uneven ends. Use fewer, larger gestures. Leave substantial areas of the face, hair and torso unworked. The sense of a face emerges from selected marks rather than continuous modelling. Subtle organic irregularity; not cartoonish and not vector art.

Likeness: the actual young Jackie in the photos, early twenties; distinctive thick eyebrows, eyes, straight nose, mouth and natural jaw shape, centre part, long hair past both shoulders, narrow moustache and a small short chin beard. Preserve these proportions and characteristic asymmetries. No generic handsome rock-star replacement, no beautifying, no large full beard.
Face: accurately place eyes, nostrils and mouth using a few decisive strokes; leave the forehead mostly a quiet open area; describe cheek and nose shadow using sparse irregular hatching with gaps, not photographic gradients or solid polygonal patches. Do NOT completely fill the face with fine crosshatching or smooth shading. Drawing texture comes from purposeful hand-made marks of different sizes, no all-over artificial texture.
Hair: simplify into several long gestural sweeps and large passages of untouched darkness, no mass of individually rendered fine strands. Clothes: no fabric modelling, just several broken collar and shoulder lines. Lower torso deliberately unfinished, blending into dark ground.
Composition: vertical 4:5 head-and-shoulders, head entirely within frame with breathing room; torso slightly turned, face almost frontal with gaze just toward the viewer's right, quiet alert expression. Hands out of frame. New composition, not the original hand-against-cheek pose.

CRITICAL COLOUR REQUIREMENT: NEUTRAL ACHROMATIC GREYS ONLY. Absolutely no brown, sepia, tan, cream, yellow, ochre or warm cast anywhere, including the light facial marks and background. Think black graphite and neutral grey chalk, NOT brown charcoal on antique paper. The background must visually match a dark website's flat near-black anthracite #0d0f12. All drawing marks neutral or imperceptibly cool grey, with muted medium-grey highlights around #8a8d91; darker strokes around #414448. No bright white. Gentle subdued overall contrast, like a watermark emerging from darkness. Edges fade fully into the anthracite. Avoid an obvious paper sheet or vignette border. Very little background grain.
No digital painted finish, no posterization, no embossed pebbled texture, no airbrushed gradients, no uniformly repeated hatching, no photo with a sketch filter. It should feel like a confidently abbreviated observational drawing made by an artist, loose and tactile, not a polished digital portrait.
One single drawing; no text, labels, page elements, frame, signature, logo, instruments or background scene.
